<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Cassava FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cassava" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cassava" data-question="What heavy metals are found in cassava?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in cassava?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Lead is the metal most often found at levels that matter; cadmium, arsenic and mercury are usually low or below detection in monitored cassava.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Nickel and chromium have been measured only in a few small studies, with one mining-area root reaching 2,350 µg/kg nickel.<sup class="cite">[[sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Romero-Crespo P, Jiménez-Oyola S, Salgado-Almeida B, Zambrano-Anchundia J, Goyburo-Chávez C, González-Valoys A, Higueras P · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Trace elements in farmland soils and crops, and probabilistic health risk assessment in areas influenced by mining activity in Ecuador</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ezema2023-evaluation-of-pesticide-residues-and-heavy-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">AuthorS: Kingsley O. Omeje in common food tubers from Nigeria Benjamin O. Ezema, Sabinus O.O. Eze AFFILIAtIoNS: Pesticide residues · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ezema2023-evaluation-of-pesticide-residues-and-heavy-metals">Evaluation of pesticide residues and heavy metals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ezema2023-evaluation-of-pesticide-residues-and-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Albishi TS, Adaigho D, Alqahtani NK, Sami R, Uguru H, Helal M, Alaoufi SH, Alkaltham MS, Osiga-Aibangbee D, Okolotu GI, Emumejaye EP, Qari SH · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">In vitro evaluation of bio-fortification effects on the nutritional quality, toxicological safety, and antioxidant of cassava (Manihot esculenta) flour, and environmental safety of processing water, using natural additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-cassava" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-cassava" data-question="How do heavy metals get into cassava?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into cassava?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Cassava takes up metals from soil, and lead can also come from soil clinging to the root or from handling after harvest.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Romero-Crespo P, Jiménez-Oyola S, Salgado-Almeida B, Zambrano-Anchundia J, Goyburo-Chávez C, González-Valoys A, Higueras P · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Trace elements in farmland soils and crops, and probabilistic health risk assessment in areas influenced by mining activity in Ecuador</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> On mining-waste soil in Ecuador cassava took up cadmium and nickel but stayed below detection for arsenic and lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Romero-Crespo P, Jiménez-Oyola S, Salgado-Almeida B, Zambrano-Anchundia J, Goyburo-Chávez C, González-Valoys A, Higueras P · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Trace elements in farmland soils and crops, and probabilistic health risk assessment in areas influenced by mining activity in Ecuador</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-forms-of-cassava-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-forms-of-cassava-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which forms of cassava have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which forms of cassava have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, starch and flour submitted from the Americas were lowest at a median of 10 µg/kg, while European tapioca of unstated form was highest at 115 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, monitored root was lowest, below 4 µg/kg median, and Nigerian flours measured 34–65 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bhunia2023-open-access-potential-toxic-levels-of-cyanide|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EDITED BY Arun K. Bhunia, Purdue University, United States REVIEWED BY Marco E. Mng&#39;ong&#39;o, sold in selected markets—taken Mbeya University of Science, Technology · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bhunia2023-open-access-potential-toxic-levels-of-cyanide">OPEN ACCESS potential toxic levels of cyanide</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bhunia2023-open-access-potential-toxic-levels-of-cyanide">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-countries-or-regions-produce-cassava-with-the-lowest-lead" data-anchor="which-countries-or-regions-produce-cassava-with-the-lowest-lead" data-question="Which countries or regions produce cassava with the lowest lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which countries or regions produce cassava with the lowest lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Cassava root submitted to GEMS/Food from the Americas had the lowest lead, a median of 9 µg/kg, against 46–92 µg/kg in European submissions.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are reporting markets, mostly of imported roots, so the evidence cannot name the producing countries with the lowest lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-foods-made-with-cassava-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="do-foods-made-with-cassava-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Do foods made with cassava also contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do foods made with cassava also contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, at levels that depend on the food: Nigerian market lafun carried 28–53 µg/kg lead, and vendor garri, fufu and amala 140–300 µg/kg on an unstated basis.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bhunia2023-open-access-potential-toxic-levels-of-cyanide|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EDITED BY Arun K. Bhunia, Purdue University, United States REVIEWED BY Marco E. Mng&#39;ong&#39;o, sold in selected markets—taken Mbeya University of Science, Technology · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bhunia2023-open-access-potential-toxic-levels-of-cyanide">OPEN ACCESS potential toxic levels of cyanide</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bhunia2023-open-access-potential-toxic-levels-of-cyanide">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/iyabo2015-ekiti-staple-foods-metals|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iyabo OO, Ogundiran MB, Adebayo OL · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/iyabo2015-ekiti-staple-foods-metals">Toxic and Essential Metals in Staple Foods Commonly Consumed by Students in Ekiti State, South West, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/iyabo2015-ekiti-staple-foods-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> One US children’s dry food made mainly from cassava flour had 44 µg/kg mercury, which its authors treated as an outlier.<sup class="cite">[[sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Charles A. Barber, Marc Boyer, Jake A. Carter, Patrick J. Gray, Jennifer Fong Sam, Mesay M. Wolle · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us">Toxic elements in baby and young children&#39;s foods in the US and correlation to ingredients</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-levels-in-cassava-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-levels-in-cassava-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the levels in cassava mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the levels in cassava mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No source in the ledger estimated exposure from cassava with verified concentrations, so the evidence cannot say how much cassava contributes to lead or cadmium intake. A Colombian study reported a cadmium hazard quotient above 1 for cassava in one municipality, but the figure cannot be reproduced from its own stated reference dose.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2023-health-risk-assessment-for-human-exposure-to-heavy|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2023-health-risk-assessment-for-human-exposure-to-heavy">Health Risk Assessment for Human Exposure to Heavy Metals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2023-health-risk-assessment-for-human-exposure-to-heavy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-cassava" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-cassava" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in cassava?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in cassava?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, for fresh root: the EU allows 0.10 mg/kg lead, 0.050 mg/kg cadmium and 0.90 mg/kg nickel in tropical roots and tubers, and Codex sets 0.1 mg/kg for lead and cadmium in root and tuber vegetables.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Neither sets a metal limit specific to cassava flour, gari or tapioca, although both regulate cyanide in those products.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-processing-reduce-heavy-metals-in-cassava" data-anchor="can-processing-reduce-heavy-metals-in-cassava" data-question="Can processing reduce heavy metals in cassava?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can processing reduce heavy metals in cassava?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Modestly, in the only measured case: soaking peeled roots in water for 48 hours lowered lead in the resulting flour by about 11% and cadmium by 8%.<sup class="cite">[[sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Albishi TS, Adaigho D, Alqahtani NK, Sami R, Uguru H, Helal M, Alaoufi SH, Alkaltham MS, Osiga-Aibangbee D, Okolotu GI, Emumejaye EP, Qari SH · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">In vitro evaluation of bio-fortification effects on the nutritional quality, toxicological safety, and antioxidant of cassava (Manihot esculenta) flour, and environmental safety of processing water, using natural additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Larger reductions with plant-extract soaks come from one laboratory lot and untested additives, so they are not an established method.<sup class="cite">[[sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Albishi TS, Adaigho D, Alqahtani NK, Sami R, Uguru H, Helal M, Alaoufi SH, Alkaltham MS, Osiga-Aibangbee D, Okolotu GI, Emumejaye EP, Qari SH · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">In vitro evaluation of bio-fortification effects on the nutritional quality, toxicological safety, and antioxidant of cassava (Manihot esculenta) flour, and environmental safety of processing water, using natural additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-cooking-cassava-get-rid-of-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-cooking-cassava-get-rid-of-heavy-metals" data-question="Does cooking cassava get rid of heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does cooking cassava get rid of heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Heat does not destroy metals, but boiling and frying lowered lead and mercury per kilogram in one study of peeled roots from Ghanaian mining towns: lead fell from 2,110 µg/kg to about 600 µg/kg when boiled and 70–80 µg/kg when fried.<sup class="cite">[[sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adjei-Mensah R, Ofori H, Tortoe C, Johnson PT, Aryee D, Frimpong SK · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops">Effect of home processing methods on the levels of heavy metal contaminants in four food crops grown in and around two mining towns in Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 8 (2021) 1830–1838</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The study did not correct for water or oil, so some of the drop may be dilution or transfer to cooking water; roasting lowered mercury least.<sup class="cite">[[sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adjei-Mensah R, Ofori H, Tortoe C, Johnson PT, Aryee D, Frimpong SK · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops">Effect of home processing methods on the levels of heavy metal contaminants in four food crops grown in and around two mining towns in Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 8 (2021) 1830–1838</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-peeling-cassava-remove-mercury" data-anchor="does-peeling-cassava-remove-mercury" data-question="Does peeling cassava remove mercury?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does peeling cassava remove mercury?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not reliably: near Ghanaian goldmines, the peeled flesh held 122–168 µg/kg mercury, and the outer skin held less than the flesh at all four sites.<sup class="cite">[[sources/adjorlologasokpoh2012-mercury-cassava-goldmines-ghana|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">A. Adjorlolo-Gasokpoh, A. A. Golow, J. Kambo-Dorsa · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/adjorlologasokpoh2012-mercury-cassava-goldmines-ghana">Mercury in the Surface Soil and Cassava, Manihot esculenta (Flesh, Leaves and Peel) Near Goldmines at Bogoso and Prestea, Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bull Environ Contam Toxicol</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/adjorlologasokpoh2012-mercury-cassava-goldmines-ghana">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Peeling remains standard practice and the EU lead and cadmium limits apply to the edible part after washing, but no study measured lead or cadmium in peel against flesh.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-soaking-cassava-overnight-help" data-anchor="does-soaking-cassava-overnight-help" data-question="Does soaking cassava overnight help?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does soaking cassava overnight help?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Soaking for 48 hours in plain water lowered flour lead and cadmium by about a tenth in a laboratory study, and the metals moved into the water.<sup class="cite">[[sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Albishi TS, Adaigho D, Alqahtani NK, Sami R, Uguru H, Helal M, Alaoufi SH, Alkaltham MS, Osiga-Aibangbee D, Okolotu GI, Emumejaye EP, Qari SH · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">In vitro evaluation of bio-fortification effects on the nutritional quality, toxicological safety, and antioxidant of cassava (Manihot esculenta) flour, and environmental safety of processing water, using natural additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Overnight soaking and traditional fermentation have not been measured for metals.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-the-cyanide-in-cassava-a-heavy-metal" data-anchor="is-the-cyanide-in-cassava-a-heavy-metal" data-question="Is the cyanide in cassava a heavy metal?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is the cyanide in cassava a heavy metal?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No; cyanide comes from natural compounds in the plant and is controlled separately, for example at 50 mg/kg in fresh peeled root and 10 mg/kg in cassava and tapioca flour in the EU.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Proper processing to remove cyanide does not by itself show anything about lead or cadmium.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="has-lead-in-cassava-been-falling" data-anchor="has-lead-in-cassava-been-falling" data-question="Has lead in cassava been falling?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Has lead in cassava been falling?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In European GEMS/Food submissions, 17 of 39 root results from 2008–2012 exceeded 100 µg/kg against 1 of 11 from 2013–2019.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are national monitoring submissions with changing coverage, not a fixed panel of producers.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-tapioca-lower-in-metals-than-cassava-root" data-anchor="is-tapioca-lower-in-metals-than-cassava-root" data-question="Is tapioca lower in metals than cassava root?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is tapioca lower in metals than cassava root?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Starch labelled as cassava or tapioca starch from the Americas was low in lead (median 10 µg/kg), similar to root from the same region.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European results labelled only “Tapioca” were higher (median 115 µg/kg), but their form is not stated, so the evidence does not show that starch is reliably lower.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-cassava-grown-near-gold-mines-higher-in-metals" data-anchor="is-cassava-grown-near-gold-mines-higher-in-metals" data-question="Is cassava grown near gold mines higher in metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is cassava grown near gold mines higher in metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, in the evidence available: cassava from Ghanaian gold-mining districts carried 120–430 µg/kg mercury near Bogoso and Kade, peeled roots from two mining towns averaged 2,110 µg/kg lead, about 30% of roots around Tarkwa had 370–450 µg/kg lead, and an Ecuadorian mining-orchard root had 60 µg/kg cadmium, above the EU limit of 50 µg/kg for tropical roots.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/adjorlologasokpoh2012-mercury-cassava-goldmines-ghana|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">A. Adjorlolo-Gasokpoh, A. A. Golow, J. Kambo-Dorsa · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/adjorlologasokpoh2012-mercury-cassava-goldmines-ghana">Mercury in the Surface Soil and Cassava, Manihot esculenta (Flesh, Leaves and Peel) Near Goldmines at Bogoso and Prestea, Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bull Environ Contam Toxicol</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/adjorlologasokpoh2012-mercury-cassava-goldmines-ghana">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adjei-Mensah R, Ofori H, Tortoe C, Johnson PT, Aryee D, Frimpong SK · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops">Effect of home processing methods on the levels of heavy metal contaminants in four food crops grown in and around two mining towns in Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 8 (2021) 1830–1838</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Romero-Crespo P, Jiménez-Oyola S, Salgado-Almeida B, Zambrano-Anchundia J, Goyburo-Chávez C, González-Valoys A, Higueras P · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Trace elements in farmland soils and crops, and probabilistic health risk assessment in areas influenced by mining activity in Ecuador</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fobi2025-boiling-cassava-cocoyam-kade-ghana|6]]<span and Cocoyam From a Gold Mining Area in Kade, Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" Ghana, and Associated Human Health Risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (2015)</span><a mining areas need lot testing rather than an assumed safe level.<sup class="cite">[[sources/adjeimensah2021-ghana-mining-home-processing-crops|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cecilia Owusu-Agyemang Fobi, Guy Eshun, Twumasi Ankrah Kwarteng, Afia Sakyiwaa Amponsah, Prince Owusu Adoma · <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-gari-and-fufu-higher-in-lead-than-cassava-root" data-anchor="are-gari-and-fufu-higher-in-lead-than-cassava-root" data-question="Are gari and fufu higher in lead than cassava root?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are gari and fufu higher in lead than cassava root?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Single vendor samples in Ado-Ekiti, Nigeria, reported 300 µg/kg lead in garri and 150 µg/kg in fufu, but the basis was not stated and the same 300 µg/kg figure is printed for six different tuber foods.<sup class="cite">[[sources/iyabo2015-ekiti-staple-foods-metals|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iyabo OO, Ogundiran MB, Adebayo OL · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/iyabo2015-ekiti-staple-foods-metals">Toxic and Essential Metals in Staple Foods Commonly Consumed by Students in Ekiti State, South West, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/iyabo2015-ekiti-staple-foods-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A garri study from Nigeria and Japan measured only chromium and nickel, with implausibly high values, so it adds no usable lead or cadmium evidence.<sup class="cite">[[sources/enyoh2023-garri-microplastics-ptes-west-africa|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Christian Ebere Enyoh, Qingyue Wang, Mominul Haque Rabin, Rasheed Oluwafemi Bakare, Joseph Longji Dadiel, Wu Shangrong, Senlin Lu, Ifenna Ilechukwu · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/enyoh2023-garri-microplastics-ptes-west-africa">Preliminary characterization and probabilistic risk assessment of microplastics and potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in garri (cassava flake), a common staple food consumed in West Africa</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Analysis Health and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/enyoh2023-garri-microplastics-ptes-west-africa">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-can-i-tell-whether-a-cassava-lead-test-is-good-enough" data-anchor="how-can-i-tell-whether-a-cassava-lead-test-is-good-enough" data-question="How can I tell whether a cassava lead test is good enough?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How can I tell whether a cassava lead test is good enough?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Check that the quantification limit is far below 100 µg/kg; laboratories reporting cassava to GEMS/Food from the Americas used 1–5 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ask for the form and basis tested, because a dry flour result and a fresh root result are not directly comparable.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Albishi TS, Adaigho D, Alqahtani NK, Sami R, Uguru H, Helal M, Alaoufi SH, Alkaltham MS, Osiga-Aibangbee D, Okolotu GI, Emumejaye EP, Qari SH · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">In vitro evaluation of bio-fortification effects on the nutritional quality, toxicological safety, and antioxidant of cassava (Manihot esculenta) flour, and environmental safety of processing water, using natural additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/albishi2026-cassava-flour-biofortification">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
